stories.title: Bangladesh reaches 302 LEED-certified factories
stories.summary: Bangladesh has reached 302 LEED-certified green factories, the highest tally globally, according to USGBC data. The total includes 134 Platinum and 148 Gold ratings, with 53 of the world's 100 highest-rated green factories now located in the country. The milestone follows 12 recent certifications for local apparel units.

stories.title: World Economic Forum ranks LC3 cement as top planetary health technology
stories.summary: The World Economic Forum has ranked LC3 cement, a blend of calcined clay and limestone, first among emerging technologies for planetary health. Developed by researchers from Cuba, Switzerland, and India, the material is intended to reduce clinker use in construction. The innovation is already being implemented in several countries.

stories.title: WEF identifies low-carbon cement as top emerging technology
stories.summary: A report from the World Economic Forum ranks LC3 cement first among emerging technologies for planetary health. The blend of calcined clay and limestone replaces a portion of the clinker used in conventional cement. Reducing clinker is a priority for lowering carbon emissions in the construction sector.

stories.title: COP31 presidency proposes buildings energy compact
stories.summary: Ministers at the UN climate summit in Antalya are expected to endorse the Antalya Compact, a plan targeting a 25 percent reduction in operational energy intensity for buildings by 2035. The proposal also aims to electrify buildings to support a 35 percent share of electricity in final energy use.

stories.title: Student team develops bio-facade for passive cooling
stories.summary: A team from MIT World Peace University has created a bio-facade using moss, algae, and cyanobacteria to reduce heat on building walls. The project, designed for Indian climates, won the Youth for Earth 2026 campaign. It aims to address rising cooling demands through passive architectural interventions.

stories.title: One of the UK's largest Passivhaus developments completed in Deptford
stories.summary: London's affordable housing supply has received a boost with the completion of 189 new homes at one of the UK's largest residential Passivhaus deve...

stories.title: Peabody completes first Passivhaus development in London
stories.summary: Peabody has finished 189 homes in Lewisham, its first residential scheme built to the Passivhaus standard. The project includes 130 homes for social rent and 59 for shared ownership. The design uses insulated walls and triple-glazed windows to reduce energy bills and carbon emissions for residents.

stories.title: Industry leaders gather to discuss wider adoption of Passivhaus
stories.summary: INDUSTRY leaders from across the UK and Ireland gathered at the Irish Embassy in London earlier this week to discuss how Passivhaus can build on it...

stories.title: Large-scale Passivhaus scheme completed in Deptford
stories.summary: Peabody and Higgins have completed a 189-home residential development in Deptford using Passivhaus fabric-first principles. The project features highly insulated envelopes and airtight construction to lower space-heating demand. The scheme highlights a growing industry interest in applying low-energy standards to large-scale residential blocks.

stories.title: Bangladesh attains historic milestone of crossing 300 LEED-certified green factories - Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)
Bangladesh crosses 300 LEED-certified green factories - Daily Sun
Bangladesh leads global LEED-certified factory count
stories.summary: Bangladesh now hosts 302 LEED-certified factories, maintaining its position as the world leader in green manufacturing facilities. Data from the US Green Building Council confirms 134 of these sites hold Platinum status. The country also claims 53 of the 100 highest-scoring green factories currently in operation.

stories.title: Design unveiled for Mumbai international cruise terminal
stories.summary: Rahul Mehta Architects has revealed the design for the Mumbai International Cruise Terminal at Indira Dock. Developed under a public-private partnership, the facility aims to integrate cruise operations with retail and public spaces. The project is intended to transform the historic waterfront into a year-round destination.

Sharjah Architecture Triennial features global practitioners
stories.summary: The third Sharjah Architecture Triennial, titled Architecture Otherwise, is currently running in the United Arab Emirates. Curated by Vyjayanthi Rao, the event brings together 35 global practitioners to explore civic infrastructure. The exhibition remains open to the public until April 14, 2027.

stories.title: Sharjah Architecture Triennial explores collective spatial knowledge
stories.summary: The third Sharjah Architecture Triennial opened in the United Arab Emirates, focusing on how collective life is shaped through spatial interactions. Curated by Vyjayanthi Rao and Tau Tavengwa, the event examines the relationship between architecture and civic infrastructure. The exhibition is scheduled to run until April 14, 2027.

stories.title: Kerala home design prioritizes landscape integration
stories.summary: Architecture studio Fictional Project has completed a home in Adoor, Kerala, featuring curving ceilings and two flanking gardens. The design, titled Interstitial Living, pulls the building volume back to create space for greenery. The studio states the residence is intended to become one with the landscape.

stories.title: MIT-WPU students develop algae-based facade to reduce heat
stories.summary: Students at MIT-WPU claim to have created an algae-based building coating that reduces surface temperatures by 3°C. Developed for a competition, the team cited urban heat islands and air conditioning dependence as motivations. Finding the correct algae for the coating proved to be the primary challenge.

stories.title: Army delays Iowa explosives detonation after public alarm
stories.summary: The U.S. Army postponed the scheduled detonation of chemicals at an Iowa ammunition plant following concerns from Illinois officials and the public regarding lead exposure. The operation, intended to destroy degraded bomb-making materials, is now set for Monday. The Army maintains the destruction is necessary for safety.

stories.title: Supreme Court quashes 388-crore demand from Gaurs Group
stories.summary: The Supreme Court rejected a 388-crore-rupee demand from the Uttar Pradesh government against Gaurs Group. The state had attempted to impose fresh commercial pricing on land used for 2,900 houses in Ghaziabad. The court also ordered a new decision regarding the allotment of low-income housing units.

stories.title: Supreme Court protects homebuyers of stalled Bengaluru project
stories.summary: The Supreme Court directed that no coercive action be taken against 4,500 homebuyers in a stalled Bengaluru project until possession is granted. The buyers have already paid 95 percent of the sale consideration to the developer, which is currently undergoing insolvency proceedings.

stories.title: Bombay HC rules on redevelopment handover
stories.summary: Mumbai-based journalist Mehul R Thakkar reports on the city's real estate landscape, noting that many residents spend little time in their homes due to long commutes. The article discusses policy, governance, and urban planning decisions within India's wealthiest civic body, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation.

stories.title: World Architecture Festival 2026 announces Day Two winners
stories.summary: The World Architecture Festival in Fort Lauderdale honored 18 additional projects on its second day. Winners across categories including Completed Buildings and Future Projects were selected by 130 international judges. The three-day event features over 400 live pitches from finalists competing for 19 awards.

stories.title: World Architecture Festival 2026 announces Day One winners
stories.summary: The World Architecture Festival began in Fort Lauderdale, announcing its first set of awards for 2026. Shortlisted projects competed across 23 categories, including Interiors and Future Projects. The event features over 400 live pitches judged by a panel of 130 international experts.

stories.title: World Architecture Festival 2026 announces Day Two winners
stories.summary: The second round of winners for the 2026 World Architecture Festival was announced in Fort Lauderdale. Finalists competed across 19 categories, including landscape and interiors. The festival features over 400 live pitches judged by 130 international experts over the course of three days.

stories.title: Lanza Atelier named as Frida Escobedo's pick for 20x20
stories.summary: Architect Frida Escobedo selected Lanza Atelier for Dezeen's 20x20 series, which highlights practitioners expected to shape the next two decades. The duo, who designed the 2026 Serpentine Pavilion, discussed their partnership and professional outlook in a sponsored interview marking the publication's 20th anniversary.

stories.title: Kengo Kuma design for National Gallery wing enters consultation
stories.summary: Kengo Kuma and Associates, working with BDP and MICA, has proposed a new wing for the National Gallery featuring Portland stone and stepped massing. The project aims to replace a 1960s office block and expand exhibition space. It remains the final stage of a 2018 masterplan.

stories.title: Bennetts Associates revitalizes Victorian hospital for university
stories.summary: London-based Bennetts Associates converted a Victorian hospital into the Edinburgh Futures Institute for the University of Edinburgh. The project, which includes a 450-seat auditorium, was shortlisted for the RIAS Andrew Doolan Best Building in Scotland Award. The revitalization focused on adapting the Category A-listed building.

stories.title: SHoP Architects designs Miami supertall skyscraper
stories.summary: SHoP Architects released designs for a 1,049-foot-tall skyscraper in Miami. The project is backed by tennis player Novak Djokovic and includes amenity facilities for the luxury brand ATMA. If completed, the tower would match the height of the in-progress Waldorf Astoria Hotel and Residences Miami.

stories.title: Sid Lee Architecture completes curved hotel in Ontario
stories.summary: Sid Lee Architecture designed The Clayfield Hotel in Niagara-on-the-Lake, a 60-room facility featuring curved glass. The 94,000-square-foot project was intended to serve as a hub for the region's wine culture. The studio stated the design takes cues from the rhythm of the vine.

stories.title: CAN completes eclectic extension for London home
stories.summary: Architecture studio CAN extended a residence in Catford, London, using concrete drainage tubes and exposed steel. The project, titled House-Tropicália, aimed to balance functional requirements for a new kitchen and bedrooms with expressive atmospheric qualities. The design was described as a very personal project.

stories.title: Design Museum hosts exhibition on Black design
stories.summary: The Design Museum in London launched The Nue Black Aesthetic, an exhibition featuring work from 16 Black designers. Guest curator Charlene Prempeh stated the show surveys the beauty and depth of Black design. It is the first time the UK has hosted an exhibition of this scope.

stories.title: Dezeen Weekly podcast reflects on 2026 award winners
stories.summary: The latest episode of the Dezeen Weekly podcast discusses the 2026 Dezeen Awards winners. The hosts also examine the construction of Donald Trump's White House ballroom, noting the project has drawn public outcry. The episode is produced by the publication's editorial team.

stories.title: COLECTIVO C733 receives inaugural Siza Award
stories.summary: Mexico-based COLECTIVO C733 was named the first recipient of the Siza Award for public architecture. The prize was established by the Serralves Foundation to honor architectural generosity and public-space engagement. The firm's portfolio includes markets, cultural facilities, and public landscapes across Mexico.

stories.title: Arctic sauna complex designed for Båtsfjord
stories.summary: Rare Collectiv has designed a sauna complex in Båtsfjord, Norway, to provide a public space for the town's international community. Located 500 kilometers above the Arctic Circle, the project aims to encourage social connection despite harsh weather conditions that often limit outdoor gatherings by the harbor.

stories.title: JSW Steel and MCi Carbon partner on waste
stories.summary: JSW Steel, MCi Carbon and JAKSON Green have signed an agreement to test the feasibility of converting steelmaking waste and carbon dioxide into low-carbon materials. The collaboration aims to reduce industrial emissions by transforming steel by-products into materials for the cement and concrete industries.

stories.title: Bamboo charcoal market projected to grow
stories.summary: Markntel Advisor reports the bamboo charcoal market was valued at USD 10.29 billion in 2026 and estimates it will reach USD 32.28 billion by 2033. The research examines demand across residential, industrial and agricultural sectors, noting an expanding role for the material in purification and personal care.

stories.title: Research team optimizes LC3 concrete
stories.summary: A research team has engineered high-strength structural concrete using modified limestone calcined clay cement. By coupling multi-criteria decision analysis with Taguchi experimental design, the study addresses historical engineering obstacles related to the complex interactions between clinker minerals, supplementary cementitious materials and chemical admixtures.

stories.title: Mass timber as an alternative to steel
stories.summary: Mass timber is an engineered wood product created by bonding layers of lumber with alternating grain directions. The method aims to provide a structural alternative to steel and concrete for tall buildings, allowing wood to be used in skyscrapers by creating panels with increased strength.

Coating method for 3D-printed polymers
stories.summary: Researchers in Finland have investigated metal and ceramic multilayer coatings to improve the durability of 3D-printed polyurethane, polypropylene and polyamide parts. The study suggests this technique could enhance surface properties while avoiding some of the hazardous chemicals typically used in conventional metal-coating processes.

stories.title: VulcanForms secures $500 million in funding
stories.summary: VulcanForms has raised $500 million, bringing its total funding to $1 billion. The company, which also received $21 million in state subsidies, intends to scale 3D-printed part production through new factories. The firm is currently attempting to dominate the market by building its own manufacturing infrastructure.

stories.title: Callaway Golf invests in titanium 3D printing
stories.summary: Callaway Golf is investing $15 million in a titanium 3D printing facility in Texas. The site is expected to begin operations in mid-2027, moving the company from prototyping to dedicated U.S. production of custom titanium products by 2028. The project expands domestic manufacturing and research capabilities.

stories.title: Kestrel Labs raises $2.13 million for AI compliance
stories.summary: Kestrel Labs has raised $2.13 million to develop an artificial intelligence platform for building code compliance. The startup aims to automate the process of checking architectural designs against regulations, a task the founders describe as an onerous part of existing design workflows.

stories.title: Kestrel Labs expands BIM integration
stories.summary: Kestrel Labs has updated its compliance platform to include integrations with Autodesk Forma and scheduled cloud checks. The software, which operates within Revit and other BIM environments, now provides a record of compliance activity and browser-based 3D review for architects managing building code requirements.

stories.title: Delhi urban heat island effect intensifies
stories.summary: Researchers at Jawaharlal Nehru University found that rapid urbanisation has turned the National Capital Region into a thermal trap. Data from 2003 to 2024 shows nocturnal heat expanding from Delhi’s core into surrounding areas, reducing the cooling relief residents once experienced after sunset.

stories.title: El Niño threatens Tamil Nadu agriculture
stories.summary: The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services reports an 80 to 100 percent probability that the current El Niño phase will persist until April 2027. Climate change is increasing baseline ocean temperatures, which may deepen water stress and threaten agricultural output in the region.

stories.title: Bhubaneswar prepares for Cyclone Akvan
stories.summary: Bhubaneswar and Cuttack have increased preparations for potential flooding as Cyclone Akvan approaches the Odisha coast. The India Meteorological Department issued an orange warning for the Khurda district, forecasting heavy rainfall and strong winds of up to 80 kmph ahead of the storm's expected landfall.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan makes landfall in Odisha
stories.summary: Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur on Friday with winds reaching 80 kmph. Authorities evacuated 3.72 lakh people, and no deaths or significant infrastructure damage were reported. The system has since weakened into a deep depression, though heavy rain is expected in parts of north Odisha.

stories.title: Heavy rain forecast following Cyclone Akvan
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department has warned of heavy to very heavy rainfall in Odisha, West Bengal and Jharkhand as Cyclone Akvan moves inland. The weather agency expects localized flooding and transport disruptions to continue through November 21 as the system weakens.

stories.title: Rain impacts Bhubaneswar and Cuttack
stories.summary: Incessant rain affected Bhubaneswar and Cuttack on Thursday as Cyclone Akvan approached the coast. Civic authorities managed localized waterlogging with pumps and personnel. Officials noted that while tree branches were damaged in some areas, the rainfall did not cause major flooding in the twin cities.

stories.title: Water supply to be cut in Suraram and Saibabanagar
stories.summary: Drinking water supply will be disrupted for 24 hours across Suraram and Saibabanagar wards starting Saturday at 9 pm. The shutdown is required to facilitate pipeline shifting works on Suraram Main Road. Residents have been advised to use water sparingly while the taps are dry.

stories.title: Flooding reported along Quirino Avenue in Davao City
stories.summary: Heavy rainfall on Thursday evening caused ankle-to-knee-deep flooding along Quirino Avenue in Davao City. Motorists and commuters have been advised to exercise caution and seek alternative routes as floodwaters continue to submerge low-lying portions of the downtown district.

stories.title: Flood watch remains in effect for South Florida
stories.summary: The National Weather Service has maintained a flood watch across Southeast Florida through Thursday evening. Meteorologists warn that additional heavy rainfall could trigger renewed urban flooding across the eastern coastal corridor, stretching from West Palm Beach down to Homestead and Flamingo.

stories.title: Deep-sea fishing vessels face design flaws in Kerala
stories.summary: Kerala received deep-sea fishing vessels under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, a government scheme launched in 2020. Fishers report that boats designed without their input are expensive to operate, turning the promise of improved livelihoods into a struggle with debt.

stories.title: Angelo Renna proposes principles for urban wildlife
stories.summary: Architect Angelo Renna has proposed eight principles for integrating non-human life into cities, shifting from development to co-evolution. The proposal follows a report stating that human activity has caused the loss of more than two-thirds of the world’s wildlife population over the last fifty years.

stories.title: Cities seek benefits from data center developers
stories.summary: Local leaders are looking for ways to protect ratepayers and control facility placement after voters expressed opposition to data centers. Municipalities are now seeking to secure meaningful benefits from developers as they respond to public pressure regarding the infrastructure projects.

stories.title: Data center project cancellations double in Q3
stories.summary: Sixteen data center projects were cancelled in the third quarter of 2026, up from seven during the same period in 2025. Climate solutions company Relae has tracked 70 such cancellations since 2024. The industry is currently facing a period of increased project attrition.

stories.title: New York City proposes fees for waste bins
stories.summary: The Department of Sanitation is proposing to charge building owners up to $55 per bin to cover installation and maintenance costs. The city is currently expanding its waste containerization program to additional neighborhoods, requiring residents to adapt to the new infrastructure.

stories.title: The paradox of smart city dashboards
stories.summary: Cities are increasingly capable of capturing and displaying urban data, such as photographing and logging potholes into municipal applications. Despite these digital tools, the problems often remain unresolved for weeks. Seeing information about an urban issue is not the same as fixing it.

stories.title: STARS Summit examines future of urban design
stories.summary: The Science, Technology, Arts and Research Summit at Dubai Future Week explored how emerging technologies can reshape cities to be more adaptable and responsive. MIT's Senseable City Lab hosted researchers and urban designers to discuss sensing, mobility, and social connectivity within the urban environment.

stories.title: Cape Town to host Global South architecture summit
stories.summary: Policymakers and industry leaders will gather in Cape Town from 23 to 24 November to discuss the shifting international order. The summit aims to ensure the Global South acts as a primary architect in the transition as post-Second World War international structures continue to unravel.

stories.title: Leratong City Mall opens in Johannesburg
stories.summary: Leratong City Mall has opened with Shoprite and Boxer as anchor tenants. The opening event featured singing and chanting from employees, reflecting the energy of the township economy. The project is being positioned as a significant development for the local retail landscape.

stories.title: Dubai uses AI to support tree planting
stories.summary: Experts at the STARS Summit are utilizing artificial intelligence to assist in the planting of 1.5 million trees across Dubai. The initiative aims to leverage technology to support the city's ongoing environmental and urban greening efforts.

stories.title: Experts call for road infrastructure decarbonisation
stories.summary: Experts at the Indian Roads Congress in Hyderabad have called for emissions to be addressed across the entire infrastructure lifecycle. Recommendations include prioritizing public transport and cycling, alongside the use of low-carbon construction materials to reduce the environmental impact of expanding road networks.

stories.title: Low-carbon materials suggested for road construction
stories.summary: Experts at the Indian Roads Congress have recommended sustainable transport planning and low-carbon materials to reduce emissions from India's road infrastructure. Suggestions for improving efficiency include the installation of roundabouts, bus bays, improved drainage, and LED lighting.

Engineers build assistive devices in Ghana
stories.summary: Engineers from Israel and Ghana have collaborated to develop pediatric rehabilitation devices using locally sourced bamboo, wood, and recycled plastic. The mission included training 40 students and conducting clinical assessments for children with disabilities to provide customized supportive braces and seating.

stories.title: Aveva and Petrojet partner on digital twin project handover
stories.summary: Aveva and Petrojet have signed a memorandum of understanding to introduce digital twin technology into industrial projects. The partnership aims to reduce inefficiencies by ensuring design and construction data remains accessible during facility operations. The software company and the contractor hope to improve operational readiness through integrated data management.

stories.title: Trimble wins two construction computing awards
stories.summary: Trimble received two awards at the 20th Construction Computing Awards in London. Tekla Structural Designer was named Structural Engineering Application of the Year for the fourth consecutive year, while Viewpoint for Projects won for document management. The awards are colloquially known as the Hammers.

stories.title: Global laser scanners market eyes 8.2 percent growth
stories.summary: The global laser scanners market is entering a phase of sustained expansion as demand for spatial data increases across construction and industrial sectors. IndexBox forecasts a compound annual growth rate of 8.2 percent through 2035, driven by a shift toward faster, higher-precision systems that integrate with digital workflows.

stories.title: Link Innovations and ChangeNOW open India hub
stories.summary: Link Innovations and ChangeNOW have launched their first hub in India at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026. The initiative aims to connect local climate and sustainability startups with global markets. Link Innovations reports having scouted over 12,000 startups and delivered 400 innovation programmes for corporate clients.

stories.title: Framery launches office pod subscription to reduce furniture waste
stories.summary: Framery is introducing an office pod subscription service to address furniture waste. The company cites data suggesting that 80 to 90 percent of office furniture in the EU is landfilled or burned, while less than one percent is recycled in the US. Pods are now available by subscription.

stories.title: Wipro emphasizes ecosystem-based architecture for AI
stories.summary: Wipro’s AI-Native Business & Platforms Unit is combining its internal platforms with technologies from partners, ranging from neo-cloud providers to frontier AI labs. Chief platform officer Hamsa Buvaraghan states that the next decade of enterprise value will be unlocked at the platform layer where intelligence meets domain execution.

stories.title: Rockwell Automation restricts AI agents to validated digital twins
stories.summary: Rockwell Automation has established rules for AI agents, limiting them to simulation tasks supported by a validated digital twin. The company uses a color-coded system to determine where virtual tests can replace physical ones. Model validation is required before any agent is permitted to chain simulation tools.

stories.title: Mechanical contractors report mixed results with BIM-to-shop links
stories.summary: While 86 percent of mechanical contractors link BIM to fabrication software, only about half report that the connection functions well. MSUITE suggests that fabrication lead times and changing install sequences often leave the shop out of the loop. The link is intended to bridge the design-to-fabrication gap.

stories.title: Spotify expands artist profile protection tool
stories.summary: Spotify has made its Artist Profile Protection tool available to all artists to combat the influx of AI-generated content. The feature allows musicians to control which releases appear on their profiles. The company says the tool addresses issues like impersonation, metadata errors, and shared names on the platform.

stories.title: Denver preserves historic elementary schools
stories.summary: Denver is using its landmark designation process to protect historic elementary schools known for their brick architecture and arched entryways. The city notes that these buildings were designed to serve as community hubs. The initiative highlights the role of school architecture in student wellbeing and local history.

stories.title: Webinar examines innovation campus design
stories.summary: A recent webinar explored how three university projects translated strategic goals into place-based design solutions. The projects focused on aligning economic opportunities and community aspirations with adaptable environments. The integrated design process aimed to foster collaboration, discovery, and long-term growth across the various campus landscapes.

stories.title: Flipped BIM course shows no impact on test scores
stories.summary: A study at Umm Al-Qura University found that a flipped learning course for Building Information Modeling resulted in no statistically significant gain in cognitive test scores. Mean scores rose from 44.98 to 45.20 points. Students reported a positive reception despite the lack of measurable improvement in objective knowledge.

stories.title: Clarion-Limestone students showcase manufacturing skills
stories.summary: Clarion-Limestone High School hosted an open house for its Lion Manufacturing program, where students demonstrated skills in welding, CNC milling, and 3D printing. The program provides student-produced parts to local businesses. It relies on grant funding and private donations to develop the next generation of manufacturers.

stories.title: Richard Murphy Architects enters liquidation
stories.summary: Richard Murphy Architects has filed a resolution to wind up after 35 years. Founder Richard Murphy cited the absence of competitions and the burden of public procurement systems as reasons for the decline. The Edinburgh-based practice, which once designed the first Maggie’s Centre, had dwindled to nine staff.

stories.title: Harvard students propose alternatives to the proposed Triumphal Arch
stories.summary: Two Harvard landscape architecture students developed conceptual designs for Memorial Circle in Washington, D.C. The proposals follow a federal judge extending an order that blocks construction of the 250-foot-tall Triumphal Arch. The site remains available for alternative ideas while the court order holds.

stories.title: When AI can answer any question, what will the teacher teach?
The Ohio State University announces Fall 2026 lecture series
stories.summary: The Knowlton School at The Ohio State University is hosting its Fall 2026 Baumer Lecture Series. The program includes speakers from various design and architectural backgrounds. The school is also currently displaying an exhibition titled Yeah, they were All Yellow: Asian Feminist Architectural Possibilities through January 22.

research.title: CERN scientists finally find evidence of a particle decay so rare it took 40 years to detect
research.summary: Scientists at CERN have found the first evidence of an incredibly rare particle decay after more than 40 years of searching, detecting a process expected to occur just once in every 10 billion beauty particles. The breakthrough could help physicists explore a mysterious microscopic realm where unknown particles.

research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Inferring relations among the units of a complex system from their activity is a fundamental problem across many fields. Here, we introduce a method to identify functional dependencies of arbitrary order from multivariate event time series. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

In particular, the renormalization flow describing how random graph models transform under node aggregation has identified a fixed point. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

Institutional and collaboration-level social media accounts are often run by professional communicators rather than by practising scientists. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
